messages:
Sarah (support): heads-up — we've got a cluster of customer tickets and a spike in PagerDuty alerts: multiple hosted-inference requests returning 5xx (mostly 503) starting ~09:12UTC. Customers see timeouts/retries failing.
Ops Bot: alert: 5xx_rate increase detected on api-gateway-prod, 5m avg x6 from baseline. top route: /v1/generate.
Liam (oncall-sre): I'm oncall, looking at traces and metrics now. Any recent deploys or config flips?
Jonah (deploy): We kicked off a canary for the new request shedder (feature flag: shedder.enable_v2) at 08:58. Canary at 5% traffic. Canary job reported healthy initially.
Natalie (platform): checking config-service and rollout logs — flag was toggled for canary group (commit abcd1234) at 08:58:12. No full rollout yet.
Matt (customer-success): Customer A sent response body from failing request: 

POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, x-customer-id: cust-A
Body: {"prompt":"hello"}

RESPONSE 503
{ "error": "gateway_timeout", "code": 503, "message": "upstream timeout while waiting for backend" }

Liam (oncall-sre): okay repro looks straightforward. I'm pulling a failing trace — gateway shows upstream call to runtime-pool timed out after 12s, followed by 503 returned to client. I also see connection resets to some runtime pods.
Jonah (deploy): interesting — shedder.v2 changes connection handling and backpressure thresholds. If it's too aggressive it might drop downstream requests causing timeouts. Did the canary config change the per-instance concurrency?
Natalie (platform): yes, shedder.v2 lowered max inflight to 8 from 32 for that canary bucket. That could easily cause queueing if burst traffic hit the 5% canary cluster.
Sarah (support): several customers reported auth-related 5xx too — any auth regressions?
Liam (oncall-sre): looking at gateway logs, I see pattern: some requests fail with 503 + log snippet "auth: token fetch ok" then immediately upstream_timeout. Not seeing 401s. So auth seems fine; the critical path is the runtime/backpressure.
Jonah (deploy): I'm going to pause the canary and immediately roll the flag back for the canary cohort. Rolling via config-service (will post commands).
Deploy Bot: rollout: canary shedder.enable_v2 -> 5% (started) commit abcd1234
Jonah (deploy): rollback steps I'm running:

# revoke the canary flag immediately
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/flags/shedder.enable_v2/rollback
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN"
  -d '{"target":"canary","action":"disable"}'

# verify
curl -s https://config.internal/api/flags/shedder.enable_v2 | jq

Jonah (deploy): sent rollback request. Waiting on config-service ack.
Ops Bot: config-service: flag update accepted (txn 8742).
Natalie (platform): Pushing a quick revert to canary routing to move traffic off the canary pool:

kubectl -n prod patch svc gateway-canary -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"rollout":"stable"}}}'

Liam (oncall-sre): I'm scaling up runtime-pool temp to absorb queued work while we stabilize:

# scale temp workers
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/runtime-pool --replicas=12

Sarah (support): I've told affected customers we're investigating and performing a rollback; asked for sample request IDs.
Matt (customer-success): Customer A confirmed errors decreased after ~2m post-rollback. They're still running some tests.
Liam (oncall-sre): metrics: 5xx rate trending down, 1m avg back to baseline ~09:18UTC. Will keep watching for error regression.
Jonah (deploy): follow-up: canary config change lowered inflight concurrency too aggressively — we missed a perf validation for bursty workloads. We'll add a quick canary test for high qps spikes to the rollout playbook.
Natalie (platform): creating patch to default concurrency to previous value for future safe rollouts. Linking PR: https://git.internal/redwood/shedder/commit/abcd1234-revert-smarter-shedder
Liam (oncall-sre): action items: 1) confirm rollback fully propagated (Natalie), 2) run soak for 30m on stable (Jonah), 3) update runbook with concurrency validation test (me + platform).
Sarah (support): I've updated customer tickets; advising retry/backoff guidance in the meantime.
Matt (customer-success): customers appreciative of quick rollback, but asked for a postmortem and ETA for a safer re-rollout.
Jonah (deploy): will schedule canary-to-stable only after adding the high-burst smoke test and running a canary for 60m.
Liam (oncall-sre): closing the alert for now; will reopen if 5xx > baseline. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Sarah (support): thanks all — keeping this thread open for postmortem notes.
Deploy Bot: rollout: canary disabled for shedder.enable_v2 (txn 8742)
